entity.summary: Global centralized cryptocurrency exchange launched July 14, 2017. In October 2026 it reported unauthorized wallet withdrawals with an initial estimated affected-asset amount of USD 6.3 billion. Withdrawals were suspended during security checks; Binance subsequently clarified that deposits remained available. Earlier November 2023 U.S. regulatory resolutions are a separate part of its historical record.
entity.notes: The October 29–30 security incident remains under investigation as of Binance's October 30 statements. Roughly USD 3B frozen on-chain is not equivalent to recovered funds; final loss and attack attribution are unverified. Binance pledged to compensate customers using both the SAFU reserve and corporate funds. Binance's homepage listed 15,000 BTC in SAFU as of February 2026; this does not establish total available corporate liquidity or a fixed compensation coverage ratio. Trading and deposits remained operational per its later clarification while withdrawals were restricted. Binance.US and Binance Japan are distinct regional scopes, not silently classified by this global incident; Binance Japan separately reported unaffected customer assets but temporarily paused crypto withdrawals.

expected.summary: Centralized exchange launched in 2017 and still operating under the Binance brand.
expected.notes: Official Binance announcement set the exchange launch for 2017-07-14.

events.title: Binance entered coordinated U.S. criminal and civil resolutions
events.description: Binance Holdings pleaded guilty to U.S. anti-money-laundering, unlicensed money-transmitting, and sanctions violations and entered coordinated resolutions with DOJ, CFTC, FinCEN, and OFAC requiring more than USD 4.3 billion in aggregate penalties and compliance remediation.
events.notes: The CFTC consent order announced on this date was initially subject to court approval; this event records the coordinated resolution announcement and Binance guilty plea rather than a service shutdown.

events.title: U.S. prosecutors reportedly opened Iran-sanctions compliance probe into Binance
events.description: Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that federal prosecutors were investigating whether Binance violated U.S. sanctions on Iran and whether it knowingly allowed prohibited trading on its platform. Reuters reported that a source confirmed the probe.
events.notes: This records a reported investigation, not a charge, adjudication, or finding that Binance violated sanctions. Reuters reported that the Justice Department declined to comment. The event does not establish a shutdown or service limitation.

events.title: Binance reports unauthorized hot-wallet withdrawals affecting approximately USD 6.3 billion
events.description: On October 29 UTC, unauthorized asset transfers affected Binance-controlled wallets. In its October 30 initial investigation, Binance estimated the total impact at approximately USD 6.3 billion and said that around USD 3 billion in affected assets had been frozen on-chain. Binance attributed a possible initial compromise to a DevOps engineer's laptop and service-container access, but said no wallet private-key leak was found. The technical root cause, final loss, attribution and recovery remain under investigation.
events.amount_text: Approximately USD 6.3 billion estimated impact; approximately USD 3 billion frozen on-chain as of the October 30 statement
events.notes: The estimated affected amount is NOT a final net stolen or unrecovered loss. EIP-7702 transaction interpretations and actor-attribution claims require separate verification; the primary Binance statement identifies an initial hypothesis, not a completed post-mortem.

events.title: Binance temporarily pauses withdrawals; later confirms deposits remained available
events.description: Following unauthorized hot-wallet transfers on October 29, Binance suspended withdrawals for security checks and revoked affected address authorization. Its initial announcement also described a temporary deposits suspension, but a later official clarification stated that deposits remained unaffected and operating normally. Trading remained possible. Binance pledged to cover customer losses with SAFU and corporate resources, but compensation completion and full withdrawals reopening had not been established in the reviewed October 30 statements.
events.notes: The service restriction is not an exchange shutdown. The initial notice's deposits-and-withdrawals phrasing was subsequently corrected by Binance; use the latest clarified state rather than perpetuating a deposit freeze. Check withdrawal reopening independently and record its date before changing the exchange from limited to active.

evidence.title: Binance and CEO Plead Guilty to Federal Charges in $4B Resolution
evidence.notes: DOJ announcement of the Binance Holdings guilty plea, financial penalty, compliance monitor, and Changpeng Zhao plea and resignation.

evidence.title: Binance and Its CEO Agree to Pay $2.85 Billion for Willfully Evading U.S. Law
evidence.notes: CFTC announcement of the proposed consent order and the coordinated aggregate resolution exceeding USD 4.3 billion.

evidence.title: Binance official exchange platform
evidence.notes: Current official domain confirming continued global exchange operation.

evidence.title: DOJ Probing Binance Over Potential Iran Sanctions Violations
evidence.notes: Reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that SDNY prosecutors and the Justice Department criminal division were examining Binance's Iran-sanctions compliance and whether prohibited trading was knowingly allowed.

evidence.title: Binance faces US scrutiny over possible Iran sanctions violations, source says
evidence.notes: Reuters reports that a source confirmed the federal probe after Bloomberg's report and notes that DOJ declined to comment. This evidence supports the existence of the reported investigation, not a finding of sanctions violations.

evidence.title: Security Incident Update
evidence.notes: Primary source for preliminary incident mechanism, USD 6.3B estimate, USD 3B frozen, and compensation pledge; not conclusive proof of final loss or root cause.

evidence.title: Binance's possible hack triggers $3 billion freeze in crypto assets
evidence.notes: Independent contemporary reporting of Binance investigation and issuer freezes; amounts are evolving estimates.

evidence.title: Security Incident Update
evidence.notes: Primary security statement originally described deposit and withdrawal suspensions; Binance subsequently clarified deposits remained operational. See the October 30 official follow-up and case report for the correction. SAFU and company funds were pledged; no payment-completion proof supplied.

evidence.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto
evidence.notes: Independent report quotes Binance spokesperson acknowledging temporary withdrawals suspension across multiple networks.
